anya: quick heads-up — ran a 1k qps perf sweep on host-proxy with the customer prompt set. host-side work (tokenization + request parse + stream chunking) is ~42% of CPU and ~55% of p50 host latency. flame snapshot below and a couple of ideas.

sam: can you paste the numbers? p50/p95 and cpu% breakdown?

anya: sure — TL;DR from pprof (aggregated across 10x 60s runs):
- total CPU: 6.2 cores avg
- tokenization: 18.6%
- request parse (proto unpack + header handling): 14.1%
- stream chunking / writev coalesce: 9.3%
- KV cache lookup + lock contended shard: 7.5%
- memcpy / copies between buffers: 6.8%
- rest (runtime, scheduler, grpc): remaining

Full snippet:```
$ pprof --text host-proxy cpu.prof
Total: 3720ms
  692ms 18.6% 18.6%  token::tokenize
  524ms 14.1% 32.7%  parse::unpack_proto
  346ms 9.3% 42.0%  stream::coalesce_writev
  279ms 7.5% 49.5%  kvcache::lookup_shard
  253ms 6.8% 56.3%  memcpy
```

jorge: interesting — those memcpy numbers match what we saw last month when we swapped to the small-chunk framing. I suspect kernel selection + batching heuristics on the GPU side are interacting: small fragments -> shorter decode -> more frequent kv lookups -> higher host churn.

mira: confirmed on my run: KV shard 3 hotness spikes at high QPS, eviction rate goes from 0.8% -> 9.7% under load. That drives extra lookup penalty + lock waits.

sam: can we do three quick experiments?
1) avoid buf copies on ingress (iovec/readv path)
2) adjust batching heuristic to prefer dynamic-batch-by-toklength (instead of flat N)
3) add a per-shard admission window to reduce eviction churn

anya: did 1) and 2) locally — results on the 60s synthetic: mean CPU down from 6.2 -> 5.1 cores, p50 host latency -18% (540ms -> 444ms), p95 host latency -9%. I swapped memcpy -> scatter-gather (readv + iovec) for proto-unpack path and added token-length-aware batch sizing that caps small-requests into slightly larger batch until a short timeout (5ms).

jorge: promising. did you measure grpc vs http tail differences?

anya: yes — with readv change grpc tail improved by ~6ms; HTTP/1.1 clients still show extra 12ms tail vs grpc (likely header parse + keepalive churn).

mira: about KV: I deployed a per-shard LRU window (size tuned to 2x median working set) and added a tiny async prefetcher when we detect repeated misses within 50ms. Eviction rate dropped to 1.5% and KV lookup p99 dropped ~22ms -> ~9ms on the same run.

sam: wow that's a big win. did anything regress on decoder kernels when you changed batching?

anya: good question — we saw a slight throughput drop on long-context batches because the dynamic heuristic was favoring larger token counts (more fusion), so the kernel selector fell back to unfused-attn for some shapes. I pushed a kernel selection tweak: prefer fused kernel when avg_seq_len <= 128 and batch_size_effective >= 4. After tweak, end-to-end throughput restored and host cpu stayed low.

jorge: any flaky regressions in canary?

anya: rolled to 5% pool for 30 minutes: no increased error rate, latency improved across the board. Observability: added metric host_ingress.memcpy_ops and kvcache.shard_hit_rate per shard.

infra-bot: deployment 2026-03-23T10:12Z started for host-proxy-canary (5% nodes).

deploy-bot: canary passed healthchecks at 5% -> promoting to 20% over 10m window. ping @mira for rollback safety-net.

mira: will keep an eye. I also created a dashboard with per-shard eviction and hit-rate + p99 lookup latency.

anya: next steps:
- roll batching/kernelselect tweak to dedicated column and run 2-hour soak under mixed loads
- add a light-weight zero-copy path to http1 header parsing (follow-up PR)
- add automated regression test in perf infra that asserts host-side CPU% < 35% at 1k qps for customer prompt set
- watch KV shard distribution and add shard-capacity alert (eviction_rate > 5% for 2m)

sam: sgtm. please open PRs and link perf graphs. can we also run one run with --kernel-debug to collect kernel selection traces?

anya: yes — I'll attach traces and the exact perf job id once it's uploaded (job: host-proxy-perf-20260323-17).

jorge: thanks all — nice cross-stack win, especially the small zero-copy + KV window combo. :party_parrot:

anya: TY — will post PR + flamegraphs here.
